sentences.text: The Petitioners in M.V.C. No.5976/2021, 5977/2021 5978/2021 & 5979/2021 have filed the Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ each for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Since all these Petitions arises out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 2204 2022 in MVC No.5976/2021, these all cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 13112021 at about 1.30 a.m. the Petitioners were proceeding in a 407 Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA183582 and the driver Mr.Maganna Gowda drove his vehicle slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road from Yalahanka towards Hebbala, near Colombia Asia hospital, BB Road, at that time, the driver of the Toyota Etios Car bearing Reg.No.KA50A4038 came in a rash and negligent manner and with high speed and dashed to the goods vehicle in which the petitioners were proceeding.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioners of all the petitions had sustained severe injuries.

4. Immediately after the accident, all the Petitioners have been shifted to Colombia Asia Hospital and thereafter, they shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital wherein they took treatment for their injuries.

5. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioners in MVC No.5976/2021, MVC No.5977/2021, MVC No.5978/2021 and MVC No.5979/2021 were hale and healthy and working as a Catering Service in Swati Hotel and was earning Rs.500/ per day and they were looking after their family and maintaining the house.
But, because of the injuries sustained by them, they were unable to do their work.
The Petitioners have spent an amount of Rs.50,000/ each towards treatment and medicines and Rs.25,000/ each towards conveyance etc.

6. The Petitioners of all the Petitions have averred that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Toyota Etios car bearing Reg. No.KA50A4038 which is owned by the Respondent No.2 and insured with Respondent No.1.
As such both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents in all the petitions, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective counsels.
The respondent No.1 filed its detailed Objection Statement to the main petition.
Respondent No.2 did not choose to file Objection statement.
8. In all the petitions, Respondent No.1 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.
Further it denied that the accident has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Further it denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in all the Smt.Amulu vs United India Insurance Co on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113095205/

sentences.text: It is to be noted here that according to the Petitioner, she has sustained grievous injury.

The medical record produced by the Petitioner herself i.e., Ex.P.4 Wound Certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries:
1. Lacerated wound present over left ear Pinna Scan, 1sum 2. Blunt injuries to left shoulder and chest 3. Multiple small Clarr peels left shoulder and chest 4. Swelling with wrists Further, the Doctor has opined that said injuries are simple in nature.
However, the Petitioner has not produced any documents regarding spending of money towards medical treatment.

Since, there is no document to show that injury sustained by the Petitioner in the accident is grievous in nature and in the absence of any other supporting documents, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, by considering the pain and suffering and the expenses incurred for food and conveyance, it would be proper to award global compensation of Rs.25,000/ to the Petitioner with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

26. Issue No. 2 in MVC No.5977/2021 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
It is to be noted here that according to the Petitioner, she has sustained grievous injury.

The medical record produced by the Petitioner herself i.e., Ex.P.7 Wound Certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained undisplaced at the glenoid neck of right shoulder expanding into scapula with fracture and blunt injury to the lumber spine and pelvic.
Further, the Doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
However, the Petitioner has deposed that she has spent Rs.50,000/ towards medical expenses.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced 2 medical bills at Ex.P.7 which is totally amounting to Rs.5,203/.
There is no discharge summary.

In the absence of supporting documents, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, by considering the pain and suffering and the expenses incurred for medical expenses and for food and conveyance, it would be proper to award global compensation of Rs.40,000/ to the Petitioner with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

29. Regarding Liability
: As already discussed above, in this case the driver of the offending T oyota Etios car bearing No. KA 50A4038 was chargesheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
The I.O has also charge sheeted the owner of the offending vehicle for not having FC & permit to the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
RW.1 has reiterated the Objection statement contentions in his chief affidavit.
To rebut the said evidence, neither the Respondent No.2 i.e., the owner filed his written statement nor led any evidence.
So, this clearly shows that the offending vehicle does not had Permit and FC as on the date of Accident.
